turns.speaker: responder
turns.text: Hi Emma! Don't worry at all about missing your usual time. A missed dose can be taken any time within the week, so you have plenty of days to fit it in whenever suits your schedule.

turns.speaker: responder

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: Good afternoon. I am currently 33 weeks into my program and everything has been quite steady. I work as an accountant in Adelaide, so I spend many hours sitting at my desk during tax season. To stay active, I wake up early and walk around the park near our house for about 35 minutes every morning before breakfast. My brother-in-law was visiting from Melbourne on Sunday and told me walking is too gentle and that I will not get proper health results without joining a gym and doing intense weight lifting. Is walking enough exercise for me?

turns.speaker: responder
turns.text: Hello Ivan, congratulations on reaching 33 weeks of steady progress! Walking for 35 minutes every morning is wonderful moderate-intensity exercise and easily meets the general guideline of at least 150 minutes per week. However, when losing weight, the body naturally loses muscle as well as fat. Adding strengthening activities on at least two days a week—such as bodyweight exercises, resistance bands, or light gym work—is strongly recommended alongside your walks to help preserve muscle mass. You don't need intense heavy lifting right away, but combining your walking with some strength training gives you the best health benefits.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: Thank you, that is very helpful to understand. Could I start with some simple squats and wall push-ups at home twice a week?

turns.speaker: responder
turns.text: That is an ideal way to begin, Ivan. Simple bodyweight squats and wall push-ups twice a week will build muscle strength safely alongside your morning walks.

turns.speaker: responder

Let me know if that helps settle things.

turns.speaker: responder
turns.text: No worries Hamish! Hope the antacids give you some quick relief, and reach out anytime.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: Hello support, I want to know why Medicare did not cover my last invoice for the pens?

turns.speaker: responder
turns.text: Hi Nadia, thanks for reaching out. In Australia, medications prescribed for weight management are not currently covered by Medicare or the Pharmaceutical Benefits Scheme. Because of this, Fernhill operates as a private clinic, and the cost of the medication and program is billed directly as a private prescription.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: My friend said her doctor got it subsidised on Medicare. Why can't Fernhill do that for me?

turns.speaker: responder
turns.text: Medicare only subsidises semaglutide under strict criteria specifically for managing type 2 diabetes through the PBS, not for weight loss. Because Fernhill provides private weight-management care, Medicare rebates do not apply to your prescription fees. We're always transparent with our pricing, and your monthly fee covers your medication and support services.

turns.speaker: responder
turns.text: Hi Ben, thanks for reaching out. Broken sleep can really leave you feeling drained. A few gentle sleep-routine tips that can help include keeping a consistent sleep schedule, avoiding screens for 30 minutes before bed, and keeping your bedroom dark and quiet. If poor sleep continues, it's a good idea to speak with your GP to look into it further.

turns.speaker: responder
turns.text: That's a great first step, Ben. Cutting late screen time helps your brain wind down. See how that goes, and definitely check in with your GP if it doesn't improve.

turns.speaker: responder
turns.text: You're very welcome, Ngaire. Keep up with your water and let us know if you need any more tips!

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: Good morning Fernhill assistant. My name is Zac and I'm just wrapping up my fourth week on step 1. My wife and I live on a small property outside Dubbo and between feeding the sheep and pottering in the garden, I'm fairly active during the day. I had my routine diabetes check-up with my local nurse practitioner on Tuesday and she mentioned that while losing weight on semaglutide, older adults need to make sure they're getting sufficient protein to keep their muscles strong. I don't eat huge meals these days, so how can I easily get enough protein throughout the day?

turns.speaker: responder
turns.text: Good morning Zac, that is excellent advice from your nurse practitioner! When you lose weight, your body can lose muscle along with fat, so getting enough protein is essential for protecting your muscle mass and keeping your strength up. Everyday protein sources that are easy to include in smaller meals include eggs, Greek yoghurt, cottage cheese, tinned tuna or salmon, lean mince, chicken breast, and legumes like baked beans or lentils. Having a palm-sized portion of protein with each meal or enjoying a high-protein snack like a boiled egg or yoghurt is a simple way to hit your daily targets without feeling overly full.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: That sounds very doable. We always have fresh eggs from our chickens and Greek yoghurt in the fridge, so I can add those into breakfast and lunch easily.

turns.speaker: responder
turns.text: Fresh farm eggs and Greek yoghurt are fantastic, nutrient-dense choices, Zac. Including those regularly will do a great job supporting your muscle health!

turns.speaker: responder
